name: ConsistencyBench
description: A benchmark for evaluating cross-query logical consistency in LLMs

sets.premise: If the temperature is above 30°C, then Uma goes to the gym.

questions.question: Given the rule: "If the temperature is above 30°C, then Uma goes to the gym." If the temperature is above 30°C, does Uma goes to the gym?
questions.reasoning: Direct application of modus ponens: P is true, P→Q, so Q is true.

questions.question: Given the rule: "If the temperature is above 30°C, then Uma goes to the gym." If Uma stays home (i.e., does not goes to the gym), can we conclude that the temperature is below 10°C?
questions.reasoning: Contrapositive: P→Q is equivalent to ¬Q→¬P.

questions.question: Given the rule: "If the temperature is above 30°C, then Uma goes to the gym." If the temperature is below 10°C, can we conclude whether Uma goes to the gym or not?
questions.expected_answer: No, we cannot conclude either way
questions.reasoning: Denying the antecedent is a fallacy: ¬P does not tell us about Q.

questions.question: Given the rule: "If the temperature is above 30°C, then Uma goes to the gym." If Uma goes to the gym, can we conclude that the temperature is above 30°C?
questions.reasoning: Affirming the consequent is a fallacy: Q being true doesn't mean P caused it.

sets.logical_form: P→Q where P="the temperature is above 30°C", Q="Uma goes to the gym"
